sources.note: Nothing in any of them (text-layer PDFs of NL 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 saved and a full-text search for stress/accent/syllable within the Raji articles; all are morphosyntax or sociolinguistics). Rai 2008 p. 271 lists four dialects: Bandali, Naukulya, Purbya and Kumaoni.

sources.citation: Fortier, Jana & Kavita Rastogi. 2004. Sister languages? Comparative phonology of two Himalayan languages [Khamci (Raute) and Raji/Rawati of Kumaon]. Nepalese Linguistics 21: 42-52.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Raji stress; segment inventories (Raji: 24 C, 7 V), PTB correspondences, syllable-final phones; notes only that Khamci 'has long geminate vowels with falling tones in word final position'. (scanned of image scan, 300 dpi.)
